title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (February 2027) — the year's first published revision table, and the only edition that diffs the horizon-roll forecast
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes — byte-identical to both the eia-steo-2026-12-08 lane's 2026-09-08 pull and the eia-steo-2027-01-12 lane's 2026-09-09 pull, so the page has not moved in three independent fetches). Read from the RAW HTML table rather than a converted rendering (the sibling lanes recorded a markdown converter shifting this page's Notes column by one row): the 2027 row is "February 2027 | 02/09/2027" with a blank Notes cell, and the same page states the release window as 12:00 pm-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the page's own stated rule — "the release of the STEO on the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", with the footnote "If a Federal holiday falls on the Monday before the normal release date the release is delayed until Wednesday" — whose published worked example is itself a February edition: 2027-02-04 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 02-09, and 2027-02-08 is a Monday that is not a Federal holiday (Washington's Birthday 2027 falls Monday 02-15). Filed estimate on the two standing counts every EIA entry on this calendar records, neither of them date doubt: this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting the sole prior proposal eia-steo-2027-02-09.from-eia-steo-2027-01-12.json. That proposal framed 02-09 as "the FIRST REVISION" of the newly-rolled 2028 lines and asked the owning lane to make 01-12 -> 02-09 a two-document read for national electricity consumption. BOTH halves were checked against EIA's own archived editions and they resolve in opposite directions. (1) THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS STRONGER THAN PROPOSED AND IS NOW VERIFIED. The February edition is not merely a revision — it is the year's FIRST PUBLISHED REVISION TABLE. The January edition carries NO "Notable forecast changes" section at all (verified absent in archives/jan25.pdf and archives/jan26.pdf; present in all nine other editions sampled — sep24, oct24, nov24, dec24, feb25, mar25...aug26), which is structurally necessary because a newly-added out-year has no previous forecast to diff against. February's table opens "Current forecast: February 10, 2026; previous forecast: January 13, 2026" and prints EIA's own percentage changes. So 2027-02-09 is the first document in which EIA itself states which direction the 2028 lines moved. (2) THE QUANTITATIVE PREMISE IS REFUTED: THE FIRST REVISION IS TINY. Measured on the U.S. total electricity consumption line across the full 2026 edition series, the newly-rolled 2027 forecast ran 4,364 (Jan) -> 4,372 (Feb, +0.18%) -> 4,388 -> 4,381 -> 4,379 -> 4,397 -> 4,399 -> 4,391 (Aug) billion kWh: February's first revision (+0.18%) is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the mean ordinary month (0.20%), and the whole seven-month drift is +0.62%. The 2025 pair points the other way at the same tiny scale (4,252 -> 4,239, -0.31%). The out-year electricity line is effectively fixed at first print, so the January edition IS the number for ai-energy-constraint.md and February confirms rather than revises it. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning and the tape agrees: on the only two February editions inside the 2-year window (2025-02-11, 2026-02-10) energy futures were QUIETER than an ordinary STEO day (CL=F 1.00% vs 1.34% pooled and 1.46% all-days; BZ=F 0.92%, USO 0.57%, XLE 0.46%) — the exact opposite sign to the January-edition hint eia-steo-2027-01-12 registered as FT-eia-steo-2027-01-12-3, and n=2 on both sides. Two notes for the owning lane. PUBLICATION RISK IS STRICTLY WORSE HERE THAN AT 01-12 AND THE SIBLING'S PRECEDENT DOES NOT REACH: a lapse beginning 2026-12-12 puts 2027-01-12 at day 32, inside the demonstrated 43-day 2025 envelope, but puts 2027-02-09 at DAY 60 — outside it, where EIA's own undated "short period of time" hedge (about/announcement.php, still dated January 22, 2018, re-fetched live 2026-09-09) is the only operative fact. CORRIDOR: ZERO tracked ids within +/-5 days, the emptiest of any STEO on this calendar (01-12 has three), but that number is NOT trustworthy as attribution evidence — bls.gov 403s on its 2027 schedule for the third lane running, so no 2027 CPI, jobs or PPI entry exists on this calendar at all, and the January-2027 CPI release plausibly lands within a day of 02-09. The corridor is empty of TRACKED ids, which is a statement about our coverage, not about the week.
